'''Herpetology''' was a [[Scientist/Legends|scientific]] field that included the study of [[Snake/Legends|snakes]]. During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Relan Smiff]] was awarded with the [[Herpetology Award]] by the [[Galactic Science Foundation]].<ref name="Bestiary">{{SonyCite|url=content.jsp?page=Star%20Wars%20Galaxies:%20Bestiary%20-%20Naboo|text=Star Wars Galaxies: Bestiary &ndash; Naboo}}</ref> Sometime between around [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] and [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWGdate">{{GalaxiesAED}}, and thus [[Relan Smiff]]'s research on [[fanned rawl]]s, takes place sometime between around [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] and [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]] per the reasoning [[Template:SWG timeline|here]].</ref> Smiff began to study and report that<ref name="Bestiary" /> the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo's]] [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] [[fanned rawl]]s had begun to grow larger. He reported sightings of giant fanned rawls in at least two locations and<ref name="Bestiary" /> correctly<ref name="TCSWE">{{CSWECite|I|254|fanned rawl}}</ref> believed that the snakes used the fans situated on the sides of their bodies to assist with swimming.<ref name="Bestiary" />

==Behind the scenes==
The field of herpetology was mentioned in "Star Wars Galaxies: Bestiary &ndash; Naboo," an article published on the official website for [[Sony]] Online Entertainment's [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']].<ref name="Bestiary" /> In the real world, [[Wikipedia:Herpetology|herpetology]] is a field of [[Wikipedia:Zoology|zoology]] centered around the study of [[Wikipedia:Amphibian|amphibians]] and [[Wikipedia:Reptile|reptiles]].<ref name="Herpetologist">{{WebCite|url=https://www.environmentalscience.org/career/herpetologist|text=What is a Herpetologist?|work=[https://www.environmentalscience.org/ environmentalscience.org]|archivedate=20231205214236}}</ref>
